Databricks, the U.S.-based enterprise data platform provider, announced on the 13th that it has raised $5 billion (approximately ¥800 billion) from investors including Blackstone. The company was valued at $190 billion (approximately ¥30.3 trillion). Investor enthusiasm is building around the growth of its data business, which supports enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence.

The strategic funding round was led by U.S. investment firm Coatue. In addition to Blackstone, participants included MGX, a sovereign wealth fund from the United Arab Emirates (UAE); multiple accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates and T. Rowe Price Investment Management; and new investor Sixth Street Growth.

Databricks provides a data infrastructure service that enables enterprises to centrally manage all their data—including documents and other assets—and securely leverage AI. The company indicated that the proceeds from this round will be directed toward expanding investment in products for AI agents.

The company also disclosed that its annualized recurring revenue (ARR) run rate has surpassed $7 billion (approximately ¥1.1 trillion). Revenue for the second quarter of 2026 (April–June) grew more than 80% year-over-year. As enterprise AI adoption accelerates, Databricks' business—which supports data management and AI application development—continues to expand rapidly.

Databricks competes with Snowflake, which provides cloud data warehousing services. Among analysts, the company is widely regarded as one of the most prominent private companies expected to pursue an initial public offering (IPO) in the future, alongside OpenAI and Anthropic.

This fundraising round underscores the continued flow of capital into data infrastructure companies amid the generative AI boom. As demand grows for securely connecting proprietary enterprise data to AI models, data platform providers like Databricks are positioned as the "foundation" for AI adoption, driving up their valuations among investors.

The $190 billion valuation places Databricks among the largest private technology companies in the world. The company has completed multiple large funding rounds since 2025, strengthening its presence in both capital raising and business expansion ahead of a potential IPO. The participation of Middle Eastern sovereign capital and major U.S. asset managers in this round reflects the robust global appetite for AI-related infrastructure investment.

Databricks' rapid growth reflects a structural shift in which data integration, governance, and security have become essential as enterprises deploy generative AI at scale. The company's ARR exceeding $7 billion, with growth of more than 80% year-over-year, serves as a clear indicator of the strength of this demand.

Meanwhile, competition with Snowflake is intensifying, with both companies vying to integrate data management and AI capabilities. While the timing of an IPO and market conditions remain undetermined, this large-scale fundraising has secured Databricks a financial foundation that removes any urgency to go public in the near term.
